title: Why a bug that could have threatened XRP's 100 billion supply cap stayed hidden for years
summary: The XRP Ledger Foundation said normal parameters never triggered the bug that could have broken XRP's supply cap, which is why it was undetected for years.
content: A software bug capable of threatening XRP's 100 billion supply cap remained hidden for years. title: Syfe Launches Income+ Max, Delivering Target Payouts up to 10% p.a. to Help Investors Turn Volatility into Income
summary:
Syfe, the Singapore-headquartered digital wealth platform managing over S$20 billion in assets across Asia-Pacific, today announced the launch of Income+ Max in collaboration with key Active ETF partner J.P. Morgan Asset Management and two other leading ETF managers. The multi-asset strategy addresses the biggest challenges for investors today: record-low dividend yields and extreme equity concentration, compounded by intense volatility. 
Unmanaged portfolio drift remains a hidden risk for retail investors, as evidenced by the 2022-era 60/40 allocation that crept to a stock-heavy 73/27 split by August 2026. Syfe’s multi-asset income strategy resolves this concentration risk by combining defensive multi-asset exposure with options on equities and gold – monetising short-term volatility to generate targeted yields of 8% to 10% per annum*. 
Diversified by design: Five income engines 
Income+ Max allocates across three core asset sleeves while drawing from five distinct income drivers. Each sleeve earns income a different way: coupons from the bond allocation, dividends from quality large caps, and option premiums written on the tech, small-cap and gold exposures, so no single source carries the payout.
Equities (55%): Focuses on high-quality companies with strong fundamentals and lower volatility than the broader market.
Fixed Income (35%): Maintains a short-to-medium duration profile to limit interest rate sensitivity, with credit and emerging market selection underwritten by J.P. Morgan Asset Management.
Gold (10%): Provides a structural diversifier and store of value when stocks and bonds move in tandem.
How volatility becomes income
The strategy sells call options on a portion of its equity and gold holdings and collects the premium as income. Option premiums rise when markets are uncertain, so the more volatile the environment, the more income the strategy can harvest. That premium, combined with dividends and bond coupons, is what funds the targeted 8% to 10% payout. 
Income+ Max removes the administrative complexity and cost of running a global income portfolio, with automated rebalancing and reinvesting.
The launch expands Syfe’s cash-income range, complementing the more conservative, bond-focused Income+ Preserve and Income+ Enhance portfolios.
Ritesh Ganeriwal, MD, Group Head of Investment & Advisory at Syfe, said: “Everyone’s talking about yields coming back, and bonds do pay again. But stock dividends are sitting near record lows, and chasing them means piling into the same few names as everyone else. Income+ Max goes about it differently. It earns income from market volatility itself: we write options on quality equities and gold, collect the premium and pay it out. Gold helps cushion the portfolio when markets turn, and fees are in line with passive index funds. With this launch, investors can now get cash management, bond income, multi-asset and options-based income all on Syfe.”
Ayaz Ebrahim, CEO of Singapore, South East Asia and India at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said:  “J.P. Morgan Asset Management is pleased to be a key Active ETF provider for the Syfe Income+ Max portfolio. This collaboration reflects the growing role of active ETFs in investors’ portfolios, and we look forward to leveraging our active ETF expertise to help investors pursue resilient income outcomes with transparency and accessibility.”
Income+ Max is currently being rolled out to users on the Syfe platform. To find out more: https://www.syfe.com/income-plus
* Income+ portfolios target a monthly payout range based on current market conditions. Target monthly payout is not guaranteed, and is subject to market movements. A positive payout or distribution yield does not imply a positive return. Source: Syfe, fund factsheets, as of October 2026.

title: WEX and Mastercard Partner to Launch Asia-Pacific's First Unified Fleet Payments Network
summary:
WEX and Mastercard today announced a strategic partnership set to simplify fleet management operations and modernise fleet payments across Asia-Pacific. The strategic partnership marks a first-of-its-kind initiative in the region that will drive the next-generation payments infrastructure by bringing together universal fuel, vehicle fleet maintenance, tolling, parking and more, in a single payment experience. The program is projected to process billions of dollars in annual transactions as it expands across key regional markets.
This collaboration combines Mastercard's global network, which processed 175 billion transactions in 2025, with WEX's standing as one of the world's leading issuers of virtual cards for travel payments and 40+ years of fleet management expertise. For fleet managers, fuel, maintenance, tolling and parking costs often sit across separate payment systems, making it difficult to see the full picture and creating extra work to reconcile bills. The partnership is designed to change that, helping drive daily efficiency and growth. 
Driving efficiency in the world’s fastest-growing fleet market
This strategic partnership arrives as Asia-Pacific emerges as the fastest-growing fleet management region globally. Fleet-card transaction volumes in the region are estimated at approximately US$310 billion (A$435 billion) in 2025, accounting for 31% of global volumes, and are projected to grow at 14.3% a year through 2030.
Despite this rapid expansion, fleet management operators across the region continue to face friction driven by fragmented data and siloed, legacy payment systems. 

“In 2026, the competitive advantage for fleets is found in simplicity. WEX is already a global pioneer in travel and corporate virtual payments; by joining forces with Mastercard in this new capacity, we are bringing that same engine of innovation to the APAC mobility sector,” said Matt Arthur, vice president and general manager, APAC Mobility at WEX. 
“For decades, fleets have used one card for fuel and a patchwork of systems for everything else, leaving fleet managers to stitch it all together. Together, we’re setting a new standard for a future-ready mobility ecosystem,” Ladds added.
This collaboration expands on a decades-long relationship with Mastercard, building on WEX’s position as #1 globally in volume of virtual card travel payments - powering 50% of all virtual card payments in the travel sector.

title: Mastercard Expands Its European Tech Hub in Dublin, Reinforcing Its Commitment to Europe's Digital Future
summary:
Mastercard is expanding its European Tech Hub in Dublin with the opening of a second office building at its Leopardstown campus — an innovation engine for the technologies that will power the next era of payments and commerce.
The new building, Two South County, was officially opened today by Taoiseach Micheál Martin alongside Mastercard senior executives Michael Miebach, CEO; Kelly Devine, President, Mastercard Europe; Ed McLaughlin, President and Chief Technology Officer and Ken Moore, Chief Innovation Officer.
The expansion marks a new chapter in Mastercard’s nearly 20-year presence in Ireland and in its work to build the future of payments in Europe, for Europe. Since establishing operations in Ireland in 2008 with just 36 employees, Mastercard has grown its Dublin workforce to more than 2,000 talented technologists from across the world.
Working as part of Mastercard’s global technology network, the Dublin teams have helped develop key technologies behind everyday payments made by millions of people around the world — including the tokenisation platform that powers wallet payments. With Mastercard’s continued investment in Dublin, supported by the Irish government and IDA Ireland, the teams are now playing a leading role in shaping the future of payments, from agentic commerce and quantum-resilient payments to digital security and network resilience.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin said: "The opening of Mastercard’s new office is a strong endorsement of Ireland’s reputation as a leading location for innovation, technology and digital transformation. Mastercard has played a key role in shaping the future of payments and financial technology globally, and its continued expansion in Ireland highlights the strength of our talented workforce, pro-business environment and vibrant technology ecosystem. I warmly welcome this investment and look forward to seeing Mastercard continue to innovate and grow from its Irish base in the years ahead."
"Europe has always been a driving force in payments innovation and Dublin sits at the heart of that story for Mastercard," said Ed McLaughlin, President and Chief Technology Officer at Mastercard. "From AI and cybersecurity to next-generation payments infrastructure that brings greater resilience and speed to commerce, the work happening here is helping build the future. This expansion of our European Tech Hub reflects the growth of our teams in Dublin, our confidence in Ireland's talent, and our ambitions for the years ahead."
The Dublin expansion forms part of a wider programme of investment in Europe’s digital payments future. Today, Mastercard also announced that it is:
Delivering on its commitment to expand and localise critical payments operations in Europe and has now started to process domestic transactions in France, Germany and Spain through its new European infrastructure. More countries will follow from next year, with the aim of bringing all components of local transactions into Europe by 2030.
 


Developing offline payment capabilities to enhance Europe’s payments resilience. All new Mastercard European credit and debit cards issued from next year – and all new payment terminals powered by its acquiring partners at essential retailers such as supermarkets and petrol stations – will have to support offline payments. This means people will be able to keep buying essentials during internet outages and power cuts.
Investing to keep the primary copy of intra-EEA transaction data in Europe.
Strengthening its European governance, recruiting a third independent European board member, who will serve as Chair of the Mastercard Europe Board of Directors.
"The technology developed in Dublin is helping solve real challenges for people and businesses across Europe and around the world,” said Kelly Devine, President, Mastercard Europe. “This expansion underlines our focus on turning innovation into secure, resilient payment experiences that customers can rely on.”
Michael Lohan, CEO of IDA Ireland said: “Mastercard’s decision to expand its European Tech Hub in Dublin with a new office is a strong vote of confidence in Ireland and in the talent and innovation that have supported the company’s growth here for almost 20 years. This latest investment positions the Dublin team to play an even greater role in developing exciting new technologies that will shape the future of payments, while further strengthening Ireland’s thriving financial services sector. IDA Ireland looks forward to continuing to support Mastercard as it enters this next phase of growth.”

title: Agentiq Raises $4 Million to Launch Fan-to-Athlete Investment Platform
summary:
Agentiq Sports, Inc. ("Agentiq"), the fintech platform allowing fans to indirectly invest in professional athletes' careers, today announced $4 million in funding. The round was led by defy.vc, the Silicon Valley venture firm behind multiple breakout consumer and fintech companies, and by a group led by the owner of two major European football clubs. Agentiq believes that the funding will accelerate its platform launch and allow Agentiq to scale its team and pipeline.
"For too long, being a sports fan has meant paying an entertainment tax," said Zach Kurtz, Co-Founder and CEO of Agentiq. "Betting apps, fantasy platforms, prediction markets: they all monetize your passion and give you nothing durable in return. We are building the opposite. The Agentiq platform gives fans a way to back the athletes they believe in and share in their journey. A real stake and a real connection."
Traditionally, private athlete-equity funds have operated behind closed doors, signing more than 2,000 athletes to long-term income-share agreements with limited transparency. Athletes early in their careers have had few options for accessing capital beyond traditional debt or these opaque private arrangements.
On Agentiq's platform, each athlete offering is conducted publicly through a designated series of a Delaware Series LLC. Under a Brand Advisory Agreement, the applicable Series provides the athlete with non-debt capital and brand advisory services in exchange for a defined percentage of covered future on-field Brand Income. By opening these athlete-linked offerings to everyday investors, the Agentiq platform aims to democratize investment opportunities historically dominated by private equity and other institutional counterparties. Agentiq believes its model gives athletes access to more flexible and transparent deal structures, allows them to de-risk their careers and invest in themselves, and creates a direct connection with the fans who believe in them.
Agentiq's initial athlete offerings are headlined by Justin Martinez, the 25-year-old flamethrowing closer of the Diamondbacks, and Esmerlyn Valdez, the 22-year-old Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder who has emerged as one of the most electric rookies in Major League Baseball. Through July 19, 2026, Valdez had already hit 12 home runs in 31 games. Valdez is a prime example of the type of athlete the Agentiq platform was designed for: a dynamic talent at the beginning of what could be a standout career.
In addition to Martinez and Valdez, Agentiq has signed Cardinals starting pitcher Hunter Dobbins, Ronny Cruz, Carlos Virahonda and hopes to have more than 50 athletes on the roster within the next 12 months. The company maintains a pipeline of more than 200 professional athletes across MLB, the NFL, and other major leagues.
Agentiq sits at the intersection of three compounding trends:
Fan engagement with financial products has gone mainstream. More than 40 million Americans actively use platforms like Robinhood, while Polymarket and Kalshi have normalized the idea of financial participation in real-world outcomes. Consumer demand for new, accessible ways to engage with sports has never been stronger.
The sports economy is at an all-time high. League valuations, NIL deal volume, betting handle, and prediction-market activity have all compounded for a decade. Private athlete-equity funds close 500+ deals per year, demonstrating strong demand for athlete-linked financial products.
Athletes are taking control of their economic futures. NIL reshaped college sports, and professional athletes increasingly view themselves as brands and businesses, not just players. Yet their options for non-debt capital remain limited to opaque private funds with rigid terms. Agentiq believes its model provides athletes with a transparent, fan-facing alternative.
"Fans have always wanted to feel closer to the athletes and teams they love, but there hasn't been an easy, accessible way to be part of an athlete's journey beyond simply watching and cheering them on," said Medha Agarwal, General Partner at defy.vc. "Agentiq is changing that by giving fans a new way to support athletes and share in their success over the long term. We believe Zach and Reuben have the vision and experience to build something truly new for the next generation of sports fans."
For decades, the sports industry has treated fans as a revenue source, not a stakeholder. Sports betting extracted a record $17 billion in revenue from American consumers in 2025 alone1, with sportsbooks keeping roughly 10 cents of every dollar wagered. Research shows that 95 to 97 percent of sports bettors lose money over any meaningful time period.2 Prediction markets are no better. On one of the main platforms, ordinary users have lost more than half a billion dollars since the platform launched.3 The common thread: fans pay to participate in short-duration products tied to discrete outcomes, while the house wins, and nothing of lasting value is created for most consumers.
Agentiq gives eligible fans the opportunity to indirectly invest in certain athletes' on-field careers. These SEC-qualified offerings result in ownership of securities that are freely tradable under U.S. federal securities law.
Founded by Zach Kurtz (CEO, fintech veteran, former D1 baseball player at University of Richmond, owner of a sporting products company used by 50+ pro players) and Reuben Abraham (CTO, employee 10 at Pave, former NerdWallet, UPenn Jerome Fisher M&T and Wharton '17, UAE Cricket National Team). The team includes former professional players and agents, as well as former data scientists with experience working in MLB front offices. Agentiq is headquartered in New York. For more information, visit agentiqsports.com.

title: The UK’s Digital Money Map: Regions Reveal Different Routes to Financial Progress
summary:
New analysis from Lloyds Banking Group finds that financial empowerment - having the confidence, capability and control to make informed financial decisions - has no single UK postcode. Across the country, people are using digital tools and AI for different priorities, from budgeting and debt reduction to investing, saving and planning ahead, with distinct regional patterns emerging. 
Nationally, digital tools are now a routine part of money management: across the UK nearly nine in ten (88%) users manage or track their finances digitally at least once a week. AI is also delivering reported savings, with adopters nationally estimating an average saving of £399 after following AI-powered financial recommendations. The regional picture shows how these tools are being put to work in different ways across the country. 
A different financial story in every part of the UK 
London emerges as the UK’s AI finance capital. More than three-quarters of respondents (76%) have used AI for personal finance in the past year, while 49% use it daily or weekly. Among AI users, 48% have used it for investment research. Londoners also report average savings of £562 after following AI recommendations, 41% higher (+£163) than the UK average*. However, just 75% of Londoners who use digital tools feel confident doing so - the lowest of any UK region, appearing to indicate that confidence does not arise from digital tool use alone. 
Elsewhere, digital finance serves different needs. Yorkshire and the Humber leads for budgeting and tracking spending (44%); the East Midlands for debt reduction (24%); and Wales for managing or growing investments, pensions or ISAs (23%). Scotland leads for digital cashback and credit monitoring: 39% of users use rewards apps and 38% regularly monitor their credit score, both UK highs. 
Where digital tools are delivering results 
The regional picture spans day-to-day control and longer-term ambition. In the South West, 48% of digital tool users say the tools help them feel more in control, the UK’s highest share. In the West Midlands, above-average AI use sits alongside the UK’s strongest concern about bias in AI recommendations (30%), underscoring the need for transparency and trust. 
Northern Ireland records some of the UK’s strongest reported practical outcomes among active digital tool users. Almost half (48%) say digital tools help them manage money more quickly and easily, while a third (30%) say the tools have helped them set and achieve financial goals, 12 percentage points above the UK average. Respondents also report above-average priorities around education, entrepreneurship and important life events.** 
In the North West, AI serves both immediate and future needs: 31% of AI users have used it for debt management and 44% for future financial planning. In the North East, 57% cite day-to-day expenses as a top priority, the UK’s highest share. 
Wales combines the UK’s highest reported financial engagement (87%) and knowledge (88%) with a strong long-term focus. Nearly a quarter of digital tool users (23%) say the tools have helped them manage or grow investments, pensions or ISAs, the highest share of any nation or region. 

"Financial empowerment doesn’t look the same for everyone or in every region. And place can tell us a lot about the context in which financial choices are made.  
Managing your money online should feel underpinned by tools that can adapt to the life in front of them. The opportunity is to give people useful choices and tools, the confidence to act on them, and control over the financial lives people want to lead. To me, that is true financial empowerment."
Jas SinghCEO, Consumer at Lloyds Banking Group
The findings come from Money mapped, the second in a new Spotlight series from Lloyds Banking Group's Consumer Digital Index, following Generation gains, which looked at financial empowerment across different ages and life stages. Money mapped explores how financial empowerment varies across the UK's nations and regions.
